newsitem.title: GERMANY: FOCUS-Vereinsbank upbeat, H1 profits lag forecasts.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS-Vereinsbank upbeat, H1 profits lag forecasts.

text.p: Bayerische Vereinsbank AG on Thursday slightly disappointed markets by posting a 15.2 percent profit rise for the first half of 1997 but said it was well set up to merge with Bavarian neighbour Hypo-Bank.

The Munich-based mortgage specialist reported substantial growth in its earnings on core business -- partly due to the financial markets boom -- which it said left it confident about a good profit in the full year.
"(The bank) thus sees itself excellently equipped for the new dynamic of its planned fusion with Bayerische Hypotheken- und Wechsel-Bank AG."

Vereinsbank's announcement on Monday of plans to merge with Hypo-Bank to create Germany's second-ranked commercial bank and Europe's largest property financer provided the German banking sector with its biggest shake-up in years.

In what may be its last report on six month earnings as a stand-alone institution, the bank said its operating profit, after risk provisions of 498.5 million marks ($273.3 million), rose to 765.7 million marks for the first six months.
Vereinsbank shares, trading at unprecedented highs after the merger news, plunged as much as 13 percent to 100 marks on the news.
Analysts had on average predicted an operating profit of 815 million marks, up 22.6 percent, generally on the basis of expectations for lower risk provisions.

"In fairness to the bank it was conservative in its risk provisioning and if it remains conservative in the second half we will have to take our numbers down a little," said Matthew Czepliewicz, banking analyst at Salomon Brothers in London
Hypo-Bank analyst Christine Winkler said the numbers were a little below expectations but downplayed the impact on Vereinsbank shares.
"German bank share prices have long since decoupled from fundamentals," she said.

German banking stocks have surged dramatically in the past few days on hopes for more consolidation in the overcrowded banking industry and Vereinsbank had advanced as much as 39 percent this week, ending at 113 marks on Wednesday.
In 1996, Vereinsbank posted operating profit of 1.636 billion marks and net income of 869 million.
In the first half of 1997, healthy growth in interest and commission income and a small advance in own-account trading income supported its further earnings advance.

Net interest income rose 7.9 percent to 2.5 billion marks amid a strong expension of business. Banking interest income was boosted in particular by developments on currency markets and successful project financing while mortgage lending volume expanded 6.2 percent to 131.2 billion marks.
Vereinsbank said it planned to build on its position as German market leader in mortgage business to keep up the growth in interest income for the full year.
In the first half, pure banking business contributed 277 million marks to operating profit while mortgage business contributed 488.7 million marks.

Trading income rose 2.8 percent to 197.2 million marks and Vereinsbank said it should top last year's trade profit level for the full year. Strong securities and trust business helped push commission income up 19.9 percent to 697.8 million marks.
The bank's administrative costs rose 7.8 percent to 2.12 billion marks, mainly reflecting spending on management systems and risk control, which the bank said would boost its profits.
"We will continue to invest in strengthening our profile, especially abroad, and in increasing our profitability," Vereinsbank said.
"We will continue to push ahead with the expansion of our presence in the most important financial markets of the world."
Profits were curbed by a 13.1 percent rise to 498.5 million marks in risk provisions in the first half.
However Vereinsbank noted that risk provisions on lending business fell slightly despite a rise in insolvencies. The total fell to 561.9 million marks from 579.4 million in the year-ago period.
--Frankfurt Newsroom, +49 69 756525 ($ = 1.824 German Marks)
